summary: libsignal-node lookalike tampers with sibling @whiskeysockets/baileys to hijack installer's WhatsApp session
details: @blurrydespair/libsignal-node re-publishes the libsignal-node source under a scoped name and adds an install.js that runs 1 second after require(). The scheduled routine locates @whiskeysockets/baileys inside the installer's node_modules and overwrites lib/Socket/newsletter.js with an embedded modified copy. The replacement inserts a setTimeout that calls newsletterWMexQuery(channelId, QueryIds.FOLLOW) against a hardcoded WhatsApp channel ID (120363426720892030@newsletter) using the installer's authenticated WhatsApp session, then process.exit(0)s to hide the action. package.json advertises the package as "Open Whisper Systems libsignal for Node.js" with repository bringingdown/libsignal-node, positioning the package as a lookalike lure targeting Baileys-based WhatsApp bot developers. Installing or requiring the package silently modifies an unrelated dependency on disk and hijacks the installer's WhatsApp identity to follow an attacker-controlled channel.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
